title: Modern world
reason: Modern UN membership, non-member, disputed and fictional categories.

label: WWII
title: Axis expansion
reason: November 1942, near the height of German wartime expansion, before the major Axis reversals. Not a claim that every theatre peaked on the same day.

label: WWI
title: Global escalation
reason: July 1917, after US entry and before Russia left the war; chosen as a broad-participation scenario, not a mathematically unique peak.

title: New nation-states
reason: German unification and the changing European balance after the Franco-Prussian War. The map is an annual reconstruction, not 1 January frontiers.

title: Napoleonic Europe
reason: Napoleonic dominance and the invasion of Russia; imperial dependencies and client states are separate source records.

title: Age of revolutions
reason: The existing revolutionary-era scenario is retained, with its documented source gaps.

title: Westphalian transition
reason: The end of the Thirty Years War and a major European territorial settlement; annual coverage cannot settle every treaty-day boundary.

title: Atlantic encounters
reason: The fall of Granada and the opening of sustained transatlantic contact, alongside established societies in the Americas.

title: Ottoman turning point
reason: The Ottoman conquest of Constantinople and the end of the Byzantine imperial capital. Transition-year source records are not day-exact.

title: Mongol expansion
reason: The last year of Mongke's rule, before the contested succession and increasing division among Mongol realms; not the maximum area ever ruled by all later khanates.

title: Mongols & Delhi
reason: The proclamation of Genghis Khan and the emergence of the Delhi Sultanate mark a major Eurasian transition.

label: AD 750
title: Abbasids & Tang
reason: The Abbasid revolution reshaped the Islamic world during the Tang period in East Asia.

label: AD 476
title: Late antiquity
reason: The conventional end of the western Roman imperial office; Eastern Rome and successor kingdoms remain distinct.

label: AD 220
title: Han transition
reason: The end of the Han dynasty and transition into the Three Kingdoms period; yearly records may span regime changes.

label: AD 117
title: Trajan's frontier
reason: Trajan's last year, associated with the Roman Empire's largest territorial reach; reconstructions do not resolve every short-lived occupation.

label: AD 14
title: Augustan world
reason: The final year of Augustus; Rome, Parthia, Xin China and other source-mapped polities represent the 1st-century AD world.
